newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight up after 1 bln rgt payment for bills.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight up after 1 bln rgt payment for bills.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate in Malaysia rose to 6.9/7.0 percent from 5.8/6.0 after banks paid one billion ringgit for two Bank Negara bill issues, dealers said on Wednesday.
They said a slight mismatch in funds flow caused by the payment had tightened the market and pushed up the overnight rate.
The payment for the bills will be partly met by a 500 million ringgit Bank Negara bill maturing on Friday.
"It went up as high as 8.0 percent when the market opened in the afternoon. But, most of the bidders were problem names," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
In Malaysia, "problem" names are small banks and finance companies which are considered higher risk borrowers. They have to pay a premium over the regular market rates.
"Now the overnight is coming off. It may end around 6.5 percent," the dealer said.
The interbank market has been flush for the last few weeks due to maturity of long-term government bonds and overseas inflows.
Dealers said the rise in the overnight rate was unlikely to be sustained beyond Friday as the market was still very liquid.
Earlier, other interbank rates ended mostly unchanged.
One-week was at 6.60/80 percent, two week at 6.80/90 percent and three-week at 7.10/15 percent.
One-month money closed at 7.15/20 percent against 7.20/25, while three-month at 7.30/35 percent and six-month at 7.33/38 were both unchanged.
But, selling continued in interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange (MME), though volumes were lower, futures dealers said.

Around 0800 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur interbank offered rate (KLIBOR) contract for September was unchanged at 92.70, or an implied yield of 7.30 percent, while the December contract fell one point to 92.68, or 7.31 percent.
A futures dealer said the market continued to fear a rise in interest rates, particularly towards the middle of the year.
